ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Steel balls are commonly used in engineering to measure the width of small circular holes in parts. Suppose the diameter of the steel ball is 10mm, and the distance from the top of the steel ball to the surface of the part is measured to be 8mm, as shown in the figure. What is the length of the width $AB$ of this small circular hole?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, point O is the center of the circle, and through point O, draw OC$\perp$AB,\\
According to the perpendicular diameter theorem, it follows that: AC=BC,\\
$\because$The diameter is 10mm,\\
$\therefore$OA=5mm, OC=8−5=3mm,\\
In $\triangle AOC$, $\angle OCA=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $AC=\sqrt{OA^{2}-OC^{2}}=\sqrt{5^{2}-3^{2}}=4$,\\
$\therefore$AB=2AC=8mm,\\
Thus, the answer is: $AB=\boxed{8}$mm.
